verified_apis.input: Local control bytes are decoded by the adapter with a strict UTF-8 TextDecoder; JSON.parse itself accepts only a string, never bytes.
verified_apis.observable_result: object root with 7 keys, 5 objects, 3 arrays, 5 strings including an escaped \u00e9 and quotes, 5 numbers, 2 booleans, 1 null, container depth 4
verified_apis.family_note: JSON.parse is an ECMAScript builtin implemented natively in V8 14.6.202.34-node.34 inside the node binary. A V8 coverage probe of the adapter listed 84 scripts and no JSON parser script, so no parser source lines or AFL++ parser feedback are attributed. The Docker project records a narrower native signal instead: gdb function-entry hits on the unstripped binary's v8::internal::JsonParser<...> symbols (21 of 142 for the nested-object control, 0 for a node -e 0 baseline, identical on repeat, 23 for the nested-array control). Wrapper packages that call JSON.parse (parse-json, json-parse-even-better-errors, secure-json-parse, @hapi/bourne, fast-json-parse, @discoveryjs/json-ext) share this family.

unverified_documented_apis.reason: Fetch spec defines it as UTF-8 decode then the JSON.parse algorithm; same V8 family, not separately run.
Module loader path over the same JSON.parse family; not a local byte API and not run.

limit: One valid nested RFC 8259 object control (plus the fixed nested-array second control) verifies JSON.parse after strict UTF-8 decoding on Node.js 26.10.0, not every JSON variant, number range, reviver use, or BOM handling. No parser-source coverage or AFL++ feedback exists for this native path; the only feedback is per-function entry sets from gdb, which miss inlined code and say nothing about lines, blocks, or edges.
